answer_text:
Assume \(x\) is a fixed real number. Then for every integer \(k\),

\[
|\sin(kx)| \le 1.
\]

Hence

\[
\left|f_n\right|
=
\left|
\frac{e^x \sin(x)\sin(2x)\cdots \sin(nx)}{\sqrt{n}}
\right|
=
\frac{e^x}{\sqrt{n}}
\prod_{k=1}^n |\sin(kx)|
\le
\frac{e^x}{\sqrt{n}}.
\]

Since \(e^x\) is constant with respect to \(n\),

\[
\lim_{n\to\infty} \frac{e^x}{\sqrt{n}} = 0.
\]

By the squeeze theorem,

\[
\lim_{n\to\infty} f_n = 0.
\]

\[
\boxed{0}
\]

27B·v4.method: Trivial bound |sin(kx)| ≤ 1 gives |f_n| ≤ e^x/√n → 0 by squeeze, after abandoning an equidistribution-based exponential decay approach.
